entities.name: PMID:27495107
observations: Case report titled “A negative nontreponemal and/or specific antitreponemal IgM test does not exclude active infectious syphilis.”
A patient with prior latent syphilis and cerebral infarct had negative nontreponemal and specific antitreponemal IgM tests.
Treponema pallidum was detected in cerebrospinal fluid by rabbit infectivity testing; DNA subtyping identified strain type 14d/f.
Benzathine penicillin gave no apparent benefit, whereas aqueous crystalline penicillin G led to disease regression; no cerebral infarct recurrence was observed over 2 years.

The authors conclude that negative nontreponemal and/or specific antitreponemal IgM tests do not definitively exclude active infectious syphilis and that neurosyphilis should be considered when clinical findings are unexplained.

entities.name: Active infectious syphilis
observations: In the reported case, active infection was demonstrated despite negative nontreponemal and specific antitreponemal IgM tests.
The evidence specifically concerns possible central nervous system infection/neurosyphilis and should not be generalized as a standalone diagnostic rule for every patient.

entities.name: Rabbit infectivity positive
observations: Cerebrospinal fluid from a patient with negative nontreponemal and specific antitreponemal IgM tests infected a seronegative New Zealand rabbit; motile Treponema pallidum was detected and strain type 14d/f was confirmed by DNA subtyping.

entities.name: Aqueous crystalline penicillin G
observations: In the reported patient, treatment with aqueous crystalline penicillin G led to regression after benzathine penicillin provided no apparent benefit; the authors emphasize its use for neurosyphilis.
